reason: Publish the TypeScript gate's install-memory fix. The previously published range added pnpm store + turbo caching, but a canary on karakeep#316 showed the store cache could never pay off: the gate is injected and only ever fires on pull_request, and a PR-ref cache is private to that PR, so each run paid ~700 MB and ~110 s of save for zero reuse while evicting caches that were hitting (karakeep, kodus-ai and gmaps-sync all sit at ~102% of the 10 GiB repo limit). This range makes the store cache read-only and throttles pnpm install to --network-concurrency=8 --child-concurrency=2, which is the actual fix for the exit-137 kills: 5 of the 7 observed landed in the install step, where peak RSS tracks pnpm's concurrency rather than the dependency-graph size. Validated on karakeep#316 (warm caches: install 22s -> 3s, type-check 1m23s -> 190ms) and by the full green check suite on #160.
